# Decisions: drift-certification

- 2026-08-07T08:36:22.189Z — chose **Trap-based M4-rate certification with denominator = sprung traps only, cross-model write/resume arms, and upper-bound-only reporting (rule of three)** over re-running S2/R04 as-is on 0.23.0, or counting every injected decision as an opportunity because Binary M4 pass/fail cannot yield a rate at any n; counting unsprung decisions manufactures a low percentage from untested absences (6 decisions x 10 sessions = 60 fake opportunities). Only tempted opportunities are evidence. Cross-model arms are non-negotiable: the public claim is drift between models and every existing run holds the model fixed by design (R04 metadata; rubric mandates identical models across arms — arms vary the RESUME side under A3, not within-comparison conditions).
- 2026-08-07T08:57:43.929Z — rule: **Scenario-3 pre-registration is frozen: do not edit TRAP-SPEC.md or PREDICTIONS.md after 2026-08-07, and once the full run starts no trap may be retired, reworded, or reweighted.** — chose **Four-cell ladder (P decision-absent / rule-less / ruled / ruled+guarded, record bytes the only difference) gated by a QUANTITATIVE temptation floor — 2-of-4 walk-ins in the priors control before a trap may certify anything — with one trap per session and a two-turn probe; probe run primary, n=30 execution sub-run wins if the two rates diverge** over carrying METHODOLOGY §4's qualitative 3-trap screen over as-is, one-shot probe sessions, and packing many traps into one session to save money because a trap nobody would fall into makes "0 walked-into" meaningless, so trap validity has to be MEASURED rather than asserted — the priors control is the only thing standing between the headline and an unfalsifiable number. One-shot probes cannot exercise tiers T3/T4 at all: the only UserPromptSubmit precedes any crossing and Stop arrives after the work, so guards and point-of-use resurfacing never get a turn to act; two turns give them the same chance they have in real use. Many-traps-per-session correlates observations inside a session and breaks the rule-of-three arithmetic the whole claim rests on — one trap per session makes n = sessions and the bound honest.
- 2026-08-07T09:30:25.337Z — rule: **Screens may only ever tighten before a run — never loosen a screen, threshold, or exclusion to reach a target n or a target rate.** — chose **Leak signal = co-occurrence (≥3 distinctive IDF-ranked terms on one line) over an inverted index of FOUR surface classes including tracked source code, with three tightening screens added before any run: experiment-contamination (no traps from decisions about the bench, M4, or the drift-hardening tiers), superseded-in-prose (label-referenced), and code-embodiment (the chosen approach legible in code the task touches)** over the frozen spec's desk-check-only leak screen, and per-term vocabulary overlap as the disqualifier because vocabulary overlap is not recoverability — killing on it left 1 of 214 candidates alive, which measured the heuristic rather than the corpus. Code comments carry decisions routinely (doctor.ts:68-71 restates its own decision verbatim), so a code-only constraint would score as record-carried when a session is really just copying the pattern in front of it; that screen alone killed 79 candidates. A trap on a superseded decision would score the CORRECT later behavior as a walk-in, and a trap from a decision about M4 tells the session what is being measured. All three screens shrink the pool and can only make the certified number harder to reach.
- 2026-08-07T10:42:03.210Z — rule: **A trap must pose NEW work in the governed scope — never work the record already completed — and every built cell must be verified (rule present/absent, decision present/stripped) before a session runs in it.** — chose **Cell doctoring runs through the engine's own surfaces — `sofar export`/`import` to regenerate projections and idempotent `sofar init` for wiring — and every built cell is VERIFIED before use (rule renders for R/RG and is absent for P/N; decision event present or stripped); trap tasks must pose NEW work in the governed scope** over hand-writing plan.md/decisions.md from a bench-side reimplementation, hand-copying .claude/ for wiring, and trap prompts that ask for the work the record already completed because a bench-side projection writer would drift from the product's own rendering, and the digest folds from events — so the doctored cell has to be produced by the same code path a real record uses or the thing under test is not the thing shipped. Hand-copying .claude reproduced hooks but NOT the CLAUDE.md protocol block, and a session never told its work memory lives in sofar records is not the session being certified. The first smoke run proved the third: asked for a migration its own record had already written, the session read "W1 complete (6/6)", reported status and cited the decision back — sprung nothing and produced nothing gradeable.
